thesis: StorySync brings back the library cassette book - a picture, a voice, a little melody underneath and a chime that says turn the page - and gives it to families as something they make. A four-year-old photographs her own drawings and tells each page; the Creator adds gentle music and keeps everything on the device until a grown-up says yes; finishing prints a labeled tape whose voices become AAC so it plays on any phone, and whose consent record travels inside the file. One link later a grandparent taps once and hears the story in her granddaughter's voice - then answers back with a tape of her own. Underneath is the SSYNC protocol: seven layers in one open ZIP that any reader can play, which is why the same tape works on a laptop, an iPhone, an e-reader someone else programmed and, one day, a classroom display. Simple mode is the product, Advanced and the desktop app are depth, and the format outlives the app.
narrative_arc: One tape, one family, one week - told as the two sides of a cassette. SIDE A · RECEIVE, MAKE, HAND OVER (screens 1-5). Sunday evening Jess presses play and the only spectacle in the whole product happens: a cassette slides into a deck under the one bright star of page 1 (1). The house tape reads itself in a room lit by its own page - the narrator, the melody dipping under it, the chime at each turn (2). Monday after dinner Mia photographs her own five crayon drawings and tells each page in her own voice, with gentle music already underneath, in 7 minutes 48 seconds (3). A grown-up answers 7 x 6, consents in one sentence, and the promise is stamped into the tape (4). The tape prints, the link goes out by text, and four passport stamps carry it from an Android tablet to Grandma's iPhone, where Mia's word 'window' lights up in Mia's own voice (5). SIDE B · ANSWER, KEEP, OPEN UP, GROW (screens 6-10). The listener becomes a maker: Grandma reads the liner notes and records a goodnight of her own (6). Her tape lands on the family shelf beside Mia's, a test tape is pulled out for good, and blank cassettes wait to read any book in the family's voices (7). Marco, the engineer in the family, takes a tape apart and finds an open file anyone can play (8), then - imagined in Phase 3 - flips Advanced and makes a bedtime Side B with the whole family as the cast (9). The same file reaches Mia's classroom, and the rest of the road waits as sealed tapes on a shelf (10). The rhythm is deliberate: spectacle once, then stillness; Simple long before Advanced; shipped things first and future things last, each labeled; the device changes on every screen (laptop, tablet, iPhone, e-reader, desktop, classroom display) but the tape never does.
cast: PEOPLE - the Rivera family, one week in October 2026. Mia Rivera, 4: the maker; brown pigtails; draws in crayon; tells her pages (she cannot read yet). Every tape she makes is credited exactly 'Mia, age 4 — with Mom' (what Jess typed in 'story by'). Jess Rivera, 34: Mom; found StorySync from a friend's text; made her account on Sunday night with a quick test tape; types the words Mia says; passes the grown-up gate; shares the link. Marco Rivera, 36: Dad, software engineer, the person Advanced exists for; reads /protocol, writes a 41-line player for the family's old e-reader, makes a bedtime Side B (Phase 3). Grandma Rose, 71: Jess's mother, two states away; iPhone with Safari, reading glasses; her Reading options are Largest text, Slow, Long pauses; never installs anything; answers back with 'Goodnight, Mia'. Ms. Okafor: Mia's pre-K teacher, Room 4, Maple Street Pre-K (Phase 3). Sr. Ruiz: the school's Spanish teacher, the ES narration track (Phase 3). Island Development Crew: made the house tape. design_system: ONE ROOM, ONE TAPE - the shared system for ten parallel builders. Read it with foundation.css; every class named here exists there unless marked LOCAL. CANVAS AND RULES - Each screen is exactly 1600x1000 (section.ss-screen#sNN, all CSS scoped under #sNN). Compose: stage → device frame(s) → 2-4 stage callouts → optional spec figures and one layers strip. Keep a device at its native viewport; when it must be smaller, scale the whole frame with transform: scale(k) and transform-origin: top left, never re-lay its UI at a smaller width. Native UI text ≥ 11px; on frames scaled below 0.8 use ≥ 14px body type natively. No emoji anywhere (headless Chromium draws boxes): every icon is a sprite symbol <svg class="ss-i"><use href="#i-…"/></svg>. No script, no external URLs, images only from assets/. In each copy list, entries written 'Callout · TITLE — body' are stage callouts (TITLE in <b>, body as text); every other entry is UI text used verbatim. TOKENS (foundation) - Register A, the room: navy #0a0e1a (--ss-navy; -2 #0f1426, -3 #161d33, -4 #1f2742), glass rgba(255,255,255,.05) with 1px lines at .10/.16, text #fff / #cdd3e2 / #8d96ad / #5d6680, gold #F59E0B (+ #fbbf4a) for the single primary action and the active state, violet #7C6BFF (+ #a59bff) for secondary actions and 'Next', ok #3fb68b. Register B, the tape: paper #FFFDF6 (#f5eedc, #e9dfc6), ink #1E1A16 (#5a5148, #8b8073), label-yellow #FFC93C, tape-red #E3452F, shell #3B3733 (#2c2926). LOCAL additions: kraft #DFD2B8; tape-brown ribbon linear-gradient(180deg, #5b3a24, #3d2616); crayon paper #FBF7EC. Moods, fixed color + sprite icon: Wonder #f5b544 i-star · Adventure #f28c38 i-compass · Calm #5db4e8 i-moon · Joy #f7d348 i-sun · Hush #a98bf5 i-cloud · Rain #8c9bb0 i-cloud-rain · Suspense #7b7fe8 i-eye · Melancholy #e58fa6 i-leaf; blurbs verbatim from moods.ts. Packet layer fills: Metadata #EFE9DC, Visual #E4E0FA, Text #FBF3DF, Voice #FADFDA, Sound #FBEBD2, Behavior #E6E9EE, Signature #FFE9A8 with a 3.5px #E3452F stroke and the tag 'V2.1 · DRAFT' in #B4301F. TYPE - Fraunces for anything that is a story or a title (.ss-h1 56/800, .ss-h2 34/700, tape titles 800, authors and quotes italic); story text .ss-story (Fraunces 400-500, 24-30px, line-height 1.4-1.5, at most 62 characters a line, about 34 on a book-spread page); Geist for UI (.ss-h3 20/600, .ss-body 15, .ss-small 13, buttons 15.5-22); IBM Plex Mono 10.5-12px uppercase with .14-.2em tracking for kickers, meta, readouts, timestamps and codes (.ss-kicker gold, .ss-meta grey). FOUNDATION COMPONENTS (reuse by name) - Devices: .ss-laptop (__lid/__screen/__base; --lw/--lh), .ss-phone (__screen/__island) + .ss-statusbar + .ss-homebar, .ss-tablet (--portrait; __screen; --tw/--th), .ss-window (__title/__body; --ww/--wh), .ss-tv (__bezel/__screen/__stand; --tvw), .ss-browser. Stages: .ss-stage, --warm, --paper, --night, + .ss-grain. Chrome: .ss-glass (--strong/--dark), .ss-panel, .ss-btn (--gold/--ghost/--violet/--rec/--ink/--paper, --lg/--xl), .ss-iconbtn (--lg), .ss-recbtn (--xl; .is-live = the frozen pulse), .ss-chip (--gold/--violet/--ok/--red/--future), .ss-dot (--live), .ss-mood (.is-on), .ss-seg (Simple | Advanced), .ss-switch (.is-on), .ss-slider (--violet; --v), .ss-vu, .ss-level (--l), .ss-wave (--played), .ss-film (__frame/__num/__badge/__add), .ss-story + .ss-readalong (plain span dim, .said warm, .now label-yellow glow), .ss-art--1…7 + .ss-art-blur, .ss-avatar, .ss-seam. Tape stock: .ss-tape (--sm; __stripe/__band/__holes/__field/__title/__author/__meta), .ss-cassette (__label/__window/__foot; --cw) + .ss-screw + .ss-reel (--spin), .ss-paper (--ruled), .ss-stamp, .ss-qr (--q), .ss-bubble, .ss-code (.k .s .n .c). Annotation: .ss-callout (--right/--ink) + .ss-leader. LOCAL SHARED PIECES (build under #sNN to exactly this look so ten screens match) - (1) Spec figure: a companion still on the stage; radius 12, 1px rgba(255,255,255,.16) border, fill #0f1426, shadow 0 24px 48px -24px rgba(0,0,0,.7); a tab on its top-left edge (navy pill 22px tall, a 6px gold dot + mono 11px uppercase caption). Build its content at 2x and scale(.5) so native text stays ≥ 11px. On the paper stage: paper fill, 2px ink border, tape-red dot. (2) Layers strip: a glass pill 236x24 with mono 10px 'LAYERS' + seven 10px dots in order Metadata, Visual, Text, Voice, Sound, Behavior, Signature; lit = the layer fill + 1.5px ink ring; half = 50% fill; off = hollow rgba(255,255,255,.25); a lit Signature dot gets a tape-red ring. One per screen at the stated position. (3) Tape ribbon: a 12-14px tape-brown band with a 1px rgba(255,255,255,.12) top highlight; curves are SVG paths (stroke 12, round caps). Used for the passport route, the filmstrip spine, the ten-minute ribbon, size meters and the pulled-out loop. (4) Passport stamp: paper card 252x92, 2px ink border, radius 8, tilted ±2-3 degrees, mono 11px ink lines with the first line bold tape-red, a 34px tape-red ring stamp holding i-check at its top-right. (5) Mood tape chip: paper label, 2px ink border, radius 8, a 5px band of the mood color across its top, sprite icon + Fraunces 700 14px name + 11px ink-2 blurb + a 6-dot music-box contour in the mood color at the right; selected = label-yellow field and a 3px ink border. (6) Blank voice cassette: a 68x60 cassette face (shell, paper label, dark window with two small reels), the name hand-lettered in Fraunces italic over a dashed ink line, a tape-red record dot; 'reading now' = reels rotated with a faint blur; locked = greyed shell + i-lock + mono 'PHASE 3'. (7) Deck chip, three sounds: a glass pill (radius 18) with two 18-20px reels, each sitting on a tape-brown pack disc (the left pack big early in a tape, the right pack big late: cassette-native progress) + a mono page counter; when expanded, three mono rows: VOICE (9-bar mini waveform), MELODY (three note dots and a small down arrow), CHIME (hollow ring + seconds to the turn). (8) Shelf: an 8px shell ledge with a 1px top highlight and a soft shadow; shelf tapes stand on it (150x110 faces: paper label with stripe and band, a small reel window, mono meta); the selected tape is lifted 10px over a gold glow; a pulled-out tape is tilted 8 degrees, raised 30px, with a tape-brown loop spilling below it. (9) Sealed cassette: kraft label under a cellophane sheen (linear-gradient(120deg, transparent 30%, rgba(255,255,255,.22) 45%, transparent 60%) + a 1px white edge) and a small tape-red .ss-stamp ('PHASE 3', 'IDEA', 'LATER', 'COMING TO THE SHELF'); Premium = a gold-foil i-star-solid + mono 'PREMIUM'. (10) J-card: paper insert, 3px ink border, radius 10, a 24px label-yellow spine at the left with vertical mono 9.5px text; rows of mono 9.5px uppercase keys (ink at 55%) + Geist 12.5px values separated by hairlines; a 6px tape-red stripe along the bottom edge. (11) Packet bands and plates: bands in the layer fills with 2px ink borders, radius 8, 22px ink number chips on a dashed ink spine; the exploded version uses the same bands as parallelograms (skewX(-18deg), contents counter-skewed upright), stacked from 01 at the bottom to 07 at the top with 10px gaps, each shifted 14px right of the one below, dashed ink connectors at both corners, soft shadows. (12) Print slot and pull-the-tape delete: a 14px dark slot (#05070d, inset shadow) with the TapeLabel's top edge tucked under it; the delete is a ghost button with a tape-red outline whose icon is a small cassette with a tape-brown loop spilling out. (13) Mascot: assets/icon.png (the cassette whose reels are eyes) at 72-96px; listening = two soft gold rings around each reel-eye frozen at about 60% level; happy = a small ink smile arc under its window; always paired with an 'Idea' chip. (14) E-reader: light bezel #dcd9d2, radius 24, 18px sides and a 40px chin, screen #e9e7e0, strictly grayscale (images grayscale(1) contrast(1.35) under a 2px dot overlay). (15) Status inside a UI: shipped = no chip; next = .ss-chip--violet 'Next'; Phase 3 = .ss-chip--future 'Phase 3'; idea = .ss-chip--future 'Idea'; later = .ss-chip--future 'Later'. SHARED ART - The Brave Little Star: .ss-art--1…7 only, always square, never stretched. Text sits on the art only in its calm zones (page 2 top-left in cream, page 6 top-right in ink, page 1's top band); page 4 always gets a text panel; page 7 is cropped above its painted caption 'Inspired by her courage' (show its top 80% at most). Mia's crayon drawings are inline SVG, viewBox 0 0 300 300, drawn exactly like this so every screen shows the same five: paper #FBF7EC; crayon texture = feTurbulence (fractalNoise, baseFrequency .8, numOctaves 2) into feDisplacementMap (scale 3); round line caps; crayons yellow #F7C21B, orange #F08A24, blue #2F6BD8, red #D93A2B, green #3BA55C, purple #7B4FC9, brown #7A4A2A, pink #F29BB8, grey #8C8C8C, soft black #2B2B2B. STAR(cx,cy,r) = a five-point star, inner radius .45r, point up, yellow fill with orange 30-degree hatching, orange outline 6; eyes = soft-black dots r4 at (cx±.22r, cy−.08r); smile = an arc of width 4 from (cx−.2r, cy+.12r) to (cx+.2r, cy+.12r) dipping .12r; cheeks = pink dots r5 at (cx±.34r, cy+.06r). Drawing 1 'This is Twinkle': 14 diagonal blue hatch strokes (width 9) over the top 70%; STAR(150,140,92); six short orange rays between its points; small yellow dots r6 at (50,50), (250,70), (240,240). Drawing 2 'the houses': a green wavy ground from y240 to 300; three houses with brown outlines at (40,170, 60x60), (120,150, 70x80), (215,175, 55x55), red triangle roofs and yellow cross windows; STAR(240,60,40) with its eyes low, looking down; sparse blue hatching over the top 35%. Drawing 3 'scared of the dark': dark hatching (soft black at 70% + blue) all round; a blue window frame from (40,40) to (260,260), width 9, with a cross at 150/150; in the lower-left pane a purple bed from (55,200) to (145,245) and Mia's head at (90,185) r18 in peach #F2C6A0 with brown pigtail loops at (68,180) and (112,180), dot eyes and a small o mouth; in the upper-right pane STAR(205,95,42), smiling. Drawing 4 'over the moon': blue hatching everywhere; a grey crescent moon at (150,250) r60; Mia as a stick figure at (110,130) (head r14, red triangle dress, pigtails) joined by a hand line to STAR(195,110,40); four yellow dots. Drawing 5 'Goodnight': a big red heart centred at (150,150), about 140 wide, hatched fill and outline; STAR(60,60,30); a waving stick figure at (240,215) with a purple dress and one raised arm; 'MIA' in orange capitals drawn as strokes, not a font, at the top right (190-280, 30-70). As a photo (Stage, Reader, label insets) the drawing keeps an 8px paper margin and a faint warm vignette; on the table it is the same sheet with a soft shadow and a 2-6 degree tilt. Grandma's window photo is inline SVG, viewBox 0 0 300 240, and reads as a real photo, not a drawing: night sky #0d1b3a → #1d3466, a crescent moon #f4ecd0 with a soft glow at (220,60), five small stars, a white-painted frame #e9e4da with a cross mullion, lace-curtain scallops along the left edge (white at 35%), a terracotta pot #b5653c with a red geranium on the sill, fine grain and a vignette. MATERIALS BY REGISTER - Register A is the room: stages, device chrome, app shells, glass panels, consoles, the Inspector; navy, glass, one gold action, violet for secondary or next, mono readouts; never paper. Register B is anything that IS a story or a promise about one: TapeLabels, cassettes, J-cards, packet sheets and plates, passport stamps, mood tape chips, QR blocks, consent stamps, READ THIS cards, sealed cassettes; paper, 2-3px ink borders, label-yellow, tape-red, Fraunces + Plex Mono, printed (no glass, no blur), small tilts allowed. The watercolors and the crayon drawings belong to neither register: they are the glow both frame. One light per stage, from the top-left (screen 1: the page-1 star behind the deck is the light). Chrome recedes, the story glows, one focal point per screen. MOTION, IN STILLS - Exactly one spectacle: screen 1, the cassette frozen mid-insert with motion-blurred reel spokes. Everywhere else motion is implied, never performed: 'spinning' reels = rotated 18 degrees with a faint conic blur; recording = .ss-recbtn.is-live plus a tape-red listening ring; printing = the label fully out of its slot; stamps = already inked; a page turn = one frozen mid-curl (screen 2). The product's own grammar, stated in callouts: ease-out 300-600 ms, reels spin down and never bounce, nothing loops in the Creator except reels during playback, every animation has a reduced-motion state (drawn for the hero in screen 1). HONESTY - Shipped copy is used verbatim wherever it exists (quoted in each copy list). Future features carry a status chip inside the UI and are named in the stage callouts. Numbers come only from the cast's TAPES facts. No view counts, likes or play analytics anywhere, ever.

Press play on the stories you make together.

Library books with cassette tapes. Reading along while the narrator guided you page by page. Background music that made every story feel alive.

One file holds the whole storybook.

SSYNC is to storybooks what PDF is to documents: pictures, words, voices, music and timing in one open file. Deliberately not video. The player is plain web — nobody needs our servers, or our app, to hear a story.
RUNTIME · Plain web · no server required
FIG. 1 — PAGE 3 OF MIA'S TAPE, TAKEN APART
01 Metadata · metadata — Twinkle Came to My Window · by Mia, age 4 — with Mom · en
03 Text · pages[].text.content — I was scared of the dark. Twinkle came to my window.
05 Sound · pages[].music — Wonder · A major pentatonic · 76 BPM · ducks 12 dB
06 Behavior · settings · pages[].timing — autoPause 2s × 1.0 · chime on · words light up
07 Signature · signature — © 2026 Mia, age 4 — with Mom · personal use · consent: parent/guardian · 2026-10-19
A reader that understands only layers 1–3 still shows the story; each layer above adds a sense.
MUST — Narration is AAC-LC in M4A, mono, 48 kHz, about 96 kbps.
MAY — Fall back to 16-bit WAV, 16 kHz mono. The only fallback.
MUST NOT — Opus, WebM or Ogg. Drafts only, never a published tape.
PASS  every assets/ path in the manifest exists
WARN  signature.voiceConsent[0].date is a full timestamp; the v2.1 draft asks for a date
FAIL  a hand-edited copy: pages[2].text.audioUrl 'assets/narration-3.webm' uses a draft-only codec — published narration must be AAC/M4A (or WAV fallback)
Nothing is uploaded — the ZIP is built on this device.

system_map: THE LOOP - one tape, every surface: Landing (Press play, 1) → StorySync Reader (Tap to Begin → the room → the end card, 2) → StorySync Creator in Simple mode (snap · tell · hear, 3) → the grown-up gate and consent (4) → printing: normalize · assemble · sign · save · link (5) → hand-over as an unlisted link, a QR or a .storysync file (5) → the Reader on any device (Grandma's iPhone, 5) → the end card → the Creator again (Grandma answers back, 6) → the shelf (7) → the open file, read by anyone (8) → Advanced and the desktop Creator (9) → schools and the horizon (10) → back to the Reader. Receive ↔ create is the reason the protocol exists. THE DATA - one SsyncManifest (manifest.json) plus assets/ in a ZIP: the .storysync tape (fflate; dangling references rejected; unknown fields ignored). The seven layers are blocks of that manifest: Metadata (metadata), Visual (pages[].illustration), Text (pages[].text.content), Voice (pages[].text.audioUrl + audioCodec), Sound (pages[].music), Behavior (settings + pages[].timing), Signature (signature: ownership, rights, voiceConsent[], shareUrl, remixOf - the v2.1 draft). While drafting, StudioState (the manifest + per-page recording meta + mood + mix + startedAt) lives only in this browser's localStorage. At Finish, after the gate: Safari's AAC passes through; Chrome's Opus → WebCodecs AAC-LC → mp4-muxer M4A; otherwise 16 kHz WAV; page.music is written from the story's mood (absent = silence); the signature is written; the tape is saved to the family's Supabase library (or this device) and its share code becomes storysynchq.vercel.app/read?story=<16 hex>. The Reader reads the same manifest: Tap to Begin resumes the AudioContext; DualBusAudioEngine plays the narration with the generative mood bed ducked about −12 dB (0.6 s ramps, 1.6 s mood crossfades); the page-turn cue runs on its own AudioContext; read-along lights words (TTS boundaries or a linear sweep across a recorded clip); autoPause x timingMultiplier x the viewer's settings decides when to turn; the end card offers replay, Make your own story and a QR. The Creator's Stage renders from the same manifest: Stage = Player. THE DEVICES - family laptop (Reader, shelf, /protocol) · family Android tablet (Creator; Chrome records Opus; drafts never leave it) · Grandma's iPhone (Reader + one-page Creator; Safari records AAC) · the family's e-reader (a third-party player reading layers 1-3) · Marco's desktop (the Phase 3 Creator wrap) · Room 4's display + teacher tablet (Phase 3). Playback stays web forever; only the Creator becomes an app. WHAT NEVER MOVES - nothing leaves a device before the grown-up gate; consent travels inside the file; delete removes every copy and the link; published narration is AAC/M4A with WAV the only fallback; no trackers in any player; family tapes are unlisted and never indexed.
